{{short description|Element in Riemannian geometry}}

In the mathematical field of [[Riemannian geometry]], every [[submanifold]] of a [[Riemannian manifold]] has a [[surface area]]. The '''first variation of area formula''' is a fundamental computation for how this quantity is affected by the deformation of the submanifold. The fundamental quantity is to do with the [[mean curvature]]. 

Let {{math|(''M'', ''g'')}} denote a Riemannian manifold, and consider an oriented smooth manifold {{mvar|S}} (possibly with boundary) together with a one-parameter family of smooth [[Immersion (mathematics)|immersion]]s {{math|''f''<sub>''t''</sub>}} of {{mvar|S}} into {{mvar|M}}. For each individual value of the parameter {{mvar|t}}, the immersion {{math|''f''<sub>''t''</sub>}} induces a [[Riemannian metric]] on {{mvar|S}}, which itself induces a [[differential form]] on {{mvar|S}} known as the [[Riemannian volume form]] {{math|''&omega;''<sub>''t''</sub>}}. The ''first variation of area'' refers to the computation
:<math>\frac{d}{dt}\omega_t=-\left\langle W_t,H(f_t)\right\rangle_g\omega_t+\text{d}\left(\iota_{W_t^\parallel}\omega_t\right)</math>
in which {{math|''H''(''f''<sub>''t''</sub>)}} is the [[mean curvature|mean curvature vector]] of the immersion {{math|''f''<sub>''t''</sub>}} and {{math|''W''<sub>''t''</sub>}} denotes the ''variation vector field'' <math>\frac{\partial}{\partial t}f_t.</math> Both of these quantities are [[vector field]]s along the map {{math|''f''<sub>''t''</sub>}}. The second term in the formula represents the [[exterior derivative]] of the [[interior product]] of the volume form with the vector field <math>W_t^\parallel</math> on {{mvar|S}}, defined as the tangential projection of {{mvar|W<sub>t</sub>}}. Via [[Cartan's magic formula]], this term can also be written as the [[Lie derivative]] of the volume form relative to the tangential projection. As such, this term vanishes if each {{math|''f''<sub>''t''</sub>}} is reparametrized by the corresponding one-parameter family of diffeomorphisms of {{mvar|S}}.

Both sides of the first variation formula can be integrated over {{mvar|S}}, provided that the variation vector field has [[compact support]]. In that case it is immediate from [[Stokes' theorem]] that
:<math>\frac{d}{dt}\operatorname{vol}(f_t)=-\int_S \left\langle W_t,H(f_t)\right\rangle_g\omega_t+\int_{\partial S}\iota_{W_t^\parallel}\omega_t.</math>
In many contexts, {{mvar|S}} is a [[closed manifold]] or the variation vector field is every orthogonal to the submanifold. In either case, the second term automatically vanishes. In such a situation, the mean curvature vector is seen as entirely governing how the surface area of a submanifold is modified by a deformation of the surface. In particular, the vanishing of the mean curvature vector is seen as being equivalent to submanifold being a [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical point]] of the volume functional. This shows how a [[minimal submanifold]] can be characterized either by the critical point theory of the volume functional or by an explicit [[partial differential equation]] for the immersion.

The special case of the first variation formula arising when {{mvar|S}} is an interval on the [[real number line]] is particularly well-known. In this context, the volume functional is known as the ''length functional'' and its variational analysis is fundamental to the study of [[geodesic]]s in Riemannian geometry.
